title: Injective proper-support restriction with exact fibre range
statement: In the setting of lem-cbc-proper-support-geometric-stalk-image, the induced restriction map ((pointSmallEtale y).sheafFiber.map i ≫ c.app F) on the geometric stalk is injective, and an element of its target lies in its linear range if and only if it has proper support on the geometric fibre.

proof.text: Derive the inverse-image germ formula for module-valued sheaves directly from the point-comap and inverse-image adjunction isomorphisms. Pull back the closed support along the cartesian square; properness is stable under base change. This shows that restriction of a properly supported neighbourhood section has proper support on the geometric fibre.

For injectivity, use properSupportSectionImage to obtain the closed image of a neighbourhood section support in the base neighbourhood. If its fibre restriction is zero, an algebraic-closure point above any support point over the marked base point contradicts the germ formula. The base point therefore lies outside the closed support image, and the section has zero direct-image stalk. Monicity of i and exactness of the geometric stalk functor give the desired injectivity.

For proper morphisms, identify the geometric restriction map with the geometric exchange map using geometricFibreExchange_germs. Proper geometric-point base change makes it an isomorphism, so every fibre section lifts to a section on a pointed etale neighbourhood.

For a compactification, extend a properly supported fibre section by zero across the open immersion, use extension-by-zero base change, and lift the resulting section by proper base change on the proper ambient scheme. The open-extension support-range theorem and transport along the pullback-composition isomorphism show that its comparison image has proper support. Verify the section restriction equality using the comparison/base-change identity and adjunction units.

Over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base, the image of the proper fibre support is compact and lies in a quasi-compact open of X. Restrict to this open and apply Nagata compactification. Use the open-closed short exact sequence to lift sections vanishing outside the open into extension by zero. The proper-support composite-range theorem lifts the neighbourhood section back to the original source. Unit, counit and base-change identities show that its fibre restriction is the original section.

For an arbitrary base, choose an affine open neighbourhood of the geometric point and apply the preceding argument to the restricted morphism. The localization restriction isomorphism and the canonical pullback-pasting isomorphism transfer the lifted neighbourhood section to the original sheaf. The inverse-image germ formula transfers its support, and the composition-unit equation proves compatibility with restriction to the fibre. Finally apply hG to lift this section to G, and stalk naturality and hc identify its image with the given fibre section.
